text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croatia's state health insurance enlarges list of free medicine by 40 new medicaments.
- Dalmatia (southern Adriatic) currently hosts between 200-300 percent more tourists than last year.

- A high-ranking Serb politician has fled the U.N.-monitored Eastern Slavonia enclave in Croatia to Yugoslavia after U.N. officials arrested a Serb war crimes suspect there, says former head of joint Croat-Serb police Peter Djukic. The policitican is presumably Goran Hadzic, former leader of rebel Serbs wanted by Croatia.
- Croatia is under pressure because (President Franjo) Tudjman's policy of national interests does not suit everyone in the international community, says Tudjman's cabinet chief Hrvoje Sarinic.
- As many as 14 people died in car crashes last weekend, police say.

- We've done a good job for the future of Croatian basketball, national basketball coach Petar Skansi says after the heavily rejuvenated national side lost almost all matches at the European championship.

- The War Crimes Tribunal's indictment of former Serb mayor of Vukovar Slavko Dokmanovic, recently arrested by U.N. officials, says he 'assisted, supervised or otherwise took part' in torture and murder of patients abducted from Vukovar hospital.
- A driver of a tanker truck survived almost unscathed when his vehicle fell into a 250m deep ravine.
- The rear party of the United Nations at Zagreb airport announces the sale of leftover property, including vehicles, generators, containers. All goods payable in U.S. dollars only.
- Don't let public spending get out of control, says Robert Feldman, head of IMF's mission in Croatia.

- According to four draft amendments to Croatia's criminal code, spousal rape, torturing animals, infringing a worker's right to strike and threatening the environment will become punishable. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
